nodes.title: Sickle Cell Disease
nodes.body:
• ← (all SCD genotypes) DDx: Mandatory newborn screening and Hb Electrophoresis or HPLC in Adults.
  • Africa (Autosomal Recessive)
  • Heterozygous phenotype ↑ → MALARIA RESISTANCE
  • PATH: Stressor/Hypoxemia → Hemoglobin S polymerization → RBC sticking → Hemolysis and VENO-OCCLUSIVE CRISES (VOC)
    • COMPLICATIONS (due to VOC): Dactylitis, Acute Chest Syndrome, SCD Nephropathy, cerebrovascular accidents, (ex. strokes in children) and cognitive deficits, skeletal deform. (vs. THALASSEMIA)
    • Functional ASPLENIA (due to infarct) - spleen macrophages phagoc. OPSONIZED pathogens ∴ ↓ spleen fn = ↑ INFECTIONS and Pneumonia (↑ risk encapsulated pathogens) - need for vaccinations and PENICILLIN PROPHYLAXIS (until age 5)
  • DDx: Hemolytic anemia labs, -ve DAT, CXR w. pulmonary infiltrate
    • PBS: SICKLED cells, TARGET cells, Howell-Jolly bodies in RBCs.
  • Tx: Supportive (IV, O2, Pain control w. NSAIDs and Opiates), if Hb < 50 Transfusions, Penicillin, and HYDROXYUREA (chemotherapeutic agent found to ↑HbF), BM transplant (if eligible).
  • Note: Do NOT use COLD COMPRESS on injuries.

nodes.title: β-Thalassemia
nodes.body:
• ← YES (↑HbA2 on HPLC Chromatography?)
  • Mediterranean (Aut. Recessive)
  • PATH: ↓β = compensate by ↑α, δ, γ:
    • ↓HbA1, ↑HbA2 (Minor), ↑HbF (Major)
  • VARIANTS: MINOR (-/β) - doesn't need treatm't. Intermedia, MAJOR (-/-) aka TRANSFUSION DEPENDENT THALASSEMIA (TDT)
    • Major can be homozygous (β0) or compound heterozygous (β0β+)
    • Onset in early childhood.

nodes.title: α-Thalassemia
nodes.body:
• ← NO (Hb Gene tests needed)
  • SEA and Africa (Aut. Recessive)
  • PATH: ↓α (major forms of Hb all have α-chains ∴ major problem) - ↑β and γ chains
  • VARIANTS: Depends on # of alleles affected.
    • 1. SILENT CARRIER (-α/αα), asymptom.
    • 2. α-TRAIT (--/αα or -α/-α), mild.
    • 3 or 4 alleles affected compensate by making unique types of hemoglobin.

nodes.title: Thalassemia
nodes.body:
• → ↑HbA2 on HPLC Chromatography? → YES (β-THALASSEMIA) / NO (Hb Gene tests needed) (α-THALASSEMIA)
  • ← DECREASED GLOBIN SYNTHESIS (from MICROCYTIC ANEMIA)
  • PATH: ↓α or β chains - ↓erythropoiesis, ↓RBC stability → HEMOLYSIS → ↑EPO ∴
    • Bone Marrow expansion: EXTRAMEDULLARY HEMATOPOIESIS (w. skeletal deformities)
  • IN SEVERE THALASSEMIAS:
    • PEx: Skeletal deformities (skull, mandible), short stature, jaundice, splenomegaly, iron overload (+ hepatomegaly or cirrhosis)
      • during CHILDHOOD
  • DDx: Normal RDW, ↑ reticulocytes, ↑LDH, ↓ Haptoglobin, ↑ indirect bilirubin, Normal iron studies.
    • TARGET CELLS on PBS. HPLC Chromatography to detect Hb variants: distinguish α and β-thal. and FAMILY HISTORY / ethnicity important.
  • Tx: Transfusions, iron chelation, genetic counselling.

nodes.title: G6PD Deficiency
nodes.body:
• ← RBC ENZYMES
  • (Glucose-6-phosphate Dehydrogenase)
  • SEA, African, Mediterr. (X-linked recessive)
  • PATH: ↓ regeneration of reduced glutathione (GSH) (antioxidant) → ↑RBC oxidative stress. Oxidative stressors precipitate hemolysis by ↑ROS (Fava beans, antimalarial, sulfa drugs, infections)
  • DDx: Hemolysis labs, -ve DAT, G6PD Assays.
    • PBS: HEINZ BODIES (ROS → Hb DENATURATION), BITE CELLS (Spleen Macrophage "bite off" Hb) and BLISTER cells.
  • Tx: Avoid stressors, Folate, Splenectomy in severe cases.

nodes.title: Hemolytic Anemia
nodes.body:
• (INCREASED DESTRUCTION)
  • ← INCREASED TURNOVER (HIGH RETICULOCYTES) (from NORMOCYTIC ANEMIA)
  • → APLASTIC CRISIS secondary to INFECTION by PARVOVIRUS 19 (BM stunted, no longer compensates for hemolysis → severe anemia)
  • ↓ HAPTOGLOBIN (binding to released Hb, made in liver)
  • ↑ LDH, ↑ INDIRECT BILIRUBIN (T.Bili - Direct. Bili)
    • (Note: ↑ Direct Bilirubin is indicative of liver disease)
  • ↑EPO - ↑RETICULOCYTES
  • PEx: JAUNDICE, Scleral icterus, hemoglobinuria, hemoglobinemia, Pigmented gallstones, ± Splenomegaly.
    • INTRAVASCULAR HEMOLYSIS: MIHA, MAHA. IgM / Complement mediated destruction - ↑LDH
    • EXTRAVASCULAR HEMOLYSIS: at the SPLEEN, IgG / Opsonization - RES macrophages.
  • DDx: Start with DAT TEST, if -ve → PBS, if +ve → AIHA.

nodes.title: Warm AIHA
nodes.body:
• (1° or 2°)
  • PATH: IgG Mediated: Opsonization (Auto Abs) Phagocytosis in SPLEEN (± Splenomegaly) ∴ EXTRAVASCULAR HEMOLYSIS at 37°C
    • 1°: Idiopathic (most common)
    • 2°: Lymphoma, Lupus, Drugs (ex. Penicillin)
  • DDx: Hemolytic labs, +ve DAT (Anti-IgG > C3b)
    • PBS: SPHEROCYTES (Macrophages remove membrane - spherical)
  • Tx: Avoid triggers (heat), supportive +
    • 1. STEROIDS (ex. Prednisone) ↓ Ab production
    • 2. SPLENECTOMY (↓ Hemolysis)
    • 3. IMMUNOSUPPRESSIVES (ex. Rituximab)

nodes.title: Cold AIHA
nodes.body:
• (Acute or Chronic)
  • aka. COLD AGGLUTININ DISEASE
  • PATH: IgM Mediated: Complement (C3) fixed on RBCs ∴ INTRAVASCULAR + EXTRAVASCULAR HEMOLYSIS at 4-30°C
  • Acute: Infections (mycoplasma, mono)
  • Chronic: Lymphoma and Hepatitis
  • DDx: Hemolysis labs, +ve DAT (Anti-C3 > IgG)
    • + ↓ SERUM C3 and C4 (bc. it's being used up)
    • PBS: AGGLUTINATED RBCs
  • Tx: Avoid triggers (cold), treat underlying cause.
    • (WARM AIHA Tx is NOT effective for Cold AIHA)

nodes.title: Vitamin B9 Deficiency
nodes.body:
• (FOLATE)
  • DDx: ↑ Homocysteine, ↓ Methionine, NORMAL MMA, ↓ RBC Folic Acid levels.
  • PEx: General anemia, NO neurologic symptoms like those seen in Vit. B12 def.
  • Etiology:
    • Diet ("Tea and Toast", poverty)
    • Jejunal resection
    • Chronic alcohol use.
    • Pregnancy (↑demand)
    • HEMOLYTIC ANEMIA (↑demand)
  • Tx: SUPPLEMENTATION - ORAL
    • Treat underlying cause.

nodes.title: Folate (Vitamin B9)
nodes.body:
• 1. DNA Synthesis (dTMP)
  • 2. DNA Methylation (Methionine)
    • Embryonic Development: NEURAL TUBE DEFECTS
  • Source: Grain products and LEAFY GREENS.
  • Absorption: Mainly in JEJUNUM
  • Stored: Liver stores 3-4 MONTHS worth.

nodes.title: Functions of Vit. B9 + B12
nodes.body:
• 1. dUMP → dTMP → - - DNA Synthesis
  • FOLATE (B9) → DHF → THF → The FOLATE TRAP: S-methyl THF
    • 1. DHF → dUMP → dTMP (DHF recycled)
    • C. S-methyl THF → Recycled THF (via MTHFR Enzyme); ⊖ by Vit B12 Def, Genetic Defect
  • 2. S-methyl THF + HOMOCYSTEINE (Toxic if ↑) → METHIONINE: Need B9 and B12 (A: COBALAMIN (B12))
    • METHIONINE → Methylation Reactions (via SAM) - Silences Genes: EPIGENETICS (↓ Methylation = ↑ cell Dysplasia)
    • HOMOCYSTEINE - - → GENETIC HYPERHOMOCYSTEINEMIA
  • Fatty Acid Metabolism: PROPIONYL-CoA → METHYLMALONYL-CoA (MMA) → (MMA Mutase, B: COBALAMIN (B12)) → SUCCINYL-CoA - - → TCA (ATP Synthesis)

nodes.title: Iron Metabolism
nodes.body:
• Vit B12 absorbed in STOMACH and ILEUM
  • Fe2+ absorbed in DUODENUM and proximal jejunum
  • Folate (B9) absorbed in JEJUNUM
  • MEAT Products (↑ Bioavailability)
  • (Non-Heme) Fe3+ → (Ferrireductase, Vitamin C (↑ absorption)) → Fe2+ = HEME iron → DMT-1
  • Free ionic iron is TOXIC
  • CALCIUM ↓ iron absorption ∴ no "Tums" - calcium carbonate" to anemic pt.
  • Acidic pH of STOMACH ↑ absorption (+ VITAMIN C)
  • Hepcidin (↑ in INFLAMMATION): ⊖ by Hypoxia (HFE); ⊕ by HIGH SERUM IRON and IL-6 (from liver); Hepcidin inhibits Ferroportin
  • FERRITIN: Iron stored in enterocytes is LOST via feces when cells are shed (ex. when ↑Hepcidin due to inflam or high serum iron)
  • Fe2+ → Hephaestin → Fe3+ → Transferrin → bone marrow; Ferritin stored in liver

nodes.title: Heme Synthesis
nodes.body:
• Glycine + Succinyl-CoA → (δ-ALA-synthase) → δ-Aminolevulinic acid → (δ-ALA-dehydratase) → Porphobilinogen → Porphyrin Ring System → (Ferrochelatase) → Heme
  • δ-ALA-synthase (Vitamin B6) inhibited ⊖ by:
    • Anti-TB Drugs
    • VITAMIN B6 Deficiency
    • Alcohol Ingestion
    • Defective gene (congenital, X-linked)
  • Lead inhibits δ-ALA-dehydratase and Ferrochelatase (Lead Poisoning)

nodes.title: Iron Deficiency Anemia
nodes.body:
• PATH: ↑ loss (ex. Colon cancer w. occult GI bleeding in older adult or menorrhagia in young woman), ↓ absorption (ex. IBD, celiac or excessive breastfeeding in children - high calcium), ↑ demand (ex. Pregnancy).
  • PEx: KOILONYCHIA, PICA + general anemia features.
  • DDx: ↓ serum iron, ↓FERRITIN, ↑TRANSFERRIN,
    • ↑ Soluble Transferrin receptor (not commonly tested)
    • ↑TIBC (↓ iron saturation), ↓ RETICULOCYTES,
    • ↑RDW, ↓ Hemosiderin (Bone marrow iron)
    • ↑ PLATELETS (Reactive Thrombocytosis)
    • PBS: Microcytes (ANISOCYTOSIS ↑RDW), Severe Fe Def: ELLIPTOCYTES, TARGET Cells (rare).
  • Tx: SUPPLEMENTATION, avoid calcium, "GSF: 30-60-90" - ORAL (or IV)
    • P.O.: Side effects common.
    • IV: if p.o not tolerated or losses too high.
    • P.O.:
      • Ferrous GLUCONATE (30mg)
      • Ferrous SULPHATE (60mg)
      • Ferrous FUMARATE (90 mg)
    • (Correction of anemia in up to 3 months)

nodes.title: Sideroblastic Anemia
nodes.body:
• PATH: ↓ Protoporphyrin synthesis,
  • PEx: General anemia features
  • DDx: ↑ Iron (since not being used), ↑ Ferritin, Normal/↓ TIBC.
    • PBS: RBCs w. basophilic (RNA) STIPPLING and Pappenheimer bodies (iron granules)
    • BMS: RING SIDEROBLASTS (iron deposition in mitochondria)
  • Tx: Pyridoxine, toxin removal.

nodes.title: Lead Poisoning
nodes.body:
• PATH: See iron met. diagram.
  • PEx: Peripheral polyneuropathy (ex. wrist drop), lead lines in X-ray, cognitive impairment
  • PHx: Old homes w. lead paint, miners, children.
  • DDx: ↑ blood lead, ↑ urine δ-Aminolevulinic acid, RBC basophilic stippling on PBS.
  • Tx: Lead chelation.

nodes.body:
• ← DECREASED HEME SYNTHESIS: more commonly NORMOCYTIC
  • ← NO BONE MARROW PATHOLOGY
  • PATH: ↑IL-6 → ↑HEPCIDIN → ↓ Ferroportin activity, due to underlying infection or malignancy or autoimmune conditions (ex. IBD, Lupus).
  • DDx: ↓ Serum iron, ↑HEPCIDIN and inflamm. markers,
    • ↑ FERRITIN (↑ storage due to inhibited Ferroportin),
    • ↓ TRANSFERRIN, ↓TIBC (Normal saturation)
    • ↓ Reticulocytes, Normal RDW, Normal hemosiderin.
  • Tx: Treat underlying condition, CKD → EPO Therapy.

nodes.title: Decreased RBC Production (Normal or Low Reticulocytes)
nodes.body:
• Splenomegaly NOT usually present except in myelofibrosis and few others.
  • DDx via BM Aspiration and core biopsy
  • ↑ NO BONE MARROW PATHOLOGY → CHRONIC KIDNEY DISEASE, ANEMIA OF CHRONIC DISEASE
  • ↓ BONE MARROW PATHOLOGY (Seen on BM core biopsy)
    • ← REPLACED Bone Marrow → MYELOPHTHISIS
    • ↓ "EMPTY" Bone Marrow → PURE RED CELL APLASIA, APLASTIC ANEMIA
    • → ABNORMAL Bone Marrow → Dyserythropoietic Anemias, MYELODYSPLASTIC SYNDROME

  • Tx: EPO Injections.

nodes.title: Hematopoiesis

    • NEUPOGEN (Granulocyte CSF) from BM
    • EPO from Kidney interstitial fibroblasts
    • TPO from Liver.

nodes.title: Erythropoietin (EPO)
nodes.body:
• Hypoxia → ↑EPO from kidneys.
  • Usually ↑ in anemia
  • EPO Tx in INJECTIONS or IV
  • Tx for Anemia in AIDS patients on antivirals, Anemia w. chemotherapy, Pre-op to ↓ blood transfusions.

nodes.title: Myelophthisis
nodes.body:
• ← REPLACED Bone Marrow
  • PBS: TEAR DROPS (aka. dacrocyte RBCs).
  • BM "replaced" by various things
    • BM replaced by advanced METASTATIC SOLID CANCER
    • BM replaced by hematological cancer: LEUKEMIA or LYMPHOMA

nodes.title: Leukemia or Lymphoma
nodes.body:
• BM replaced by hematological cancer:
  • (FoM Week 11)
  • ↳ Progressive CYTOPENIAS (Anemia, Thrombocytopenia, neutropenia + symptoms)

nodes.title: Myelofibrosis
nodes.body:
• BM replaced by scarring:
  • PEx: Night Sweats w. SPLENOMEGALY (NOT seen in Aplastic Anemia) and TEAR DROPS on PBS.
  • ↓ Covered in FoM Week 11: MYELOPROLIFERATIVE DISORDERS

nodes.title: Pure Red Cell Aplasia
nodes.body:
• ← "EMPTY" Bone Marrow
  • ↓ erythroid precursors in BM w. SEVERE RETICULOCYTOPENIA
  • Congenital: Diamond Blackfan Anemia
  • Acquired: Primary (autoimmune) or Secondary (Toxins ex. chemo, radiation - infections, drugs, pregnancy)

nodes.title: Aplastic Anemia
nodes.body:
• ← "EMPTY" Bone Marrow
  • ↓ in all cell line precursors in BM w. PANCYTOPENIA and SEVERE RETICULOCYTOPENIA
    • ↓ RBCs: Anemia features (↑↑EPO)
    • ↓ Platelets: ↑ Bleeding + Bruising
    • ↓ WBCs: ↑ Recurring infections
    • (Similar Presentation to late MDS, vs.)
  • BM Biopsy: ↓ cellularity ("dry tap"), ↑ fat
  • Tx: Supportive (transfusions, antibiotics), Immunosuppression (anti-thymocyte globulin, cyclosporin, steroids), stem cell transplant if eligible

nodes.title: Dyserythropoietic Anemias
nodes.body:
• ← ABNORMAL Bone Marrow
  • (Acquired or hereditary abnormality in RBC precursors)

nodes.title: Myelodysplastic Syndrome
nodes.body:
• ← ABNORMAL Bone Marrow
  • MDS (Early) can also be a MACROCYTIC ANEMIA
  • 1 in 1000 in ELDERLY (>60 y.o)
  • "Pre-Cancer of AML"
  • Various diseases (WHO classified): INEFFECTIVE HEMATOPOIESIS in one or more cell lineages.
    • Early MDS: MACROCYTIC Anemia (mild)
    • Late MDS: Normocytic ANEMIA w. PANCYTOPENIA
      • ↳ usually neutropenia ± thrombocytopenia
  • PATH: Cells made but "die in BM" due to abnormal cell synthesis.
  • PHx: Chemotherapy, radiation, toxins
  • DDx: Bone marrow biopsy + aspirate:
    • BMS: Ring Sideroblasts, blasts, atypical HYPERPLASIA + DYSPLASIA of multiple cell lines (ex. Nuclear bridge in erythroblasts, or micro-megakaryocytes)
    • PBS: HYPOSEGMENTED NEUTROPHILS (Pseudo-Pelger-Huet Anomaly)
    • Flow Cytometry: ↑blasts (but <20%) vs. >20% in AML
    • Cytogenetics: 5q deletion or Molec. genetic tests for SF3B1 mutation.
  • Tx: TRANSFUSIONS, Antibiotics, EPO, G-CSF
    • ↳ Complication: IRON OVERLOAD (monitor via serum Ferritin)
    • Hypomethylating agents (ex. Azacytidine)
    • Goals of Tx differ based on prognosis (IPSS Score - low vs. high risk MDS)
      • ↳ BM transplants for LOW-risk MDS

nodes.title: Acute Myeloid Leukemia
nodes.body:
• Risk of conversion to ACUTE MYELOID LEUKEMIA
  • (Week 10 FoM)
  • Look for CONSTITUTIONAL symptoms, worsening of cytopenias.

nodes.title: Liver Disease
nodes.body:
• PATH: Excess lipids + cholesterol incorporated into RBC membrane.
    • → Excess membrane Projections.
    • ↳ PBS: TARGET CELLS, ACANTHOCYTES
  • Associations: Chronic ALCOHOLISM, w. nutritional deficiencies ± GI bleeds.
  • DDx: Liver Disease labs, ↑ DIRECT BILIRUBIN

nodes.title: CONGENITAL (Aplastic Anemia)
nodes.body: • (week 11 FoM)

nodes.title: Fanconi Anemia
nodes.body: • PEx: Short stature, triphalangeal thumb, skin pigmentation, w. congenital heart defects.

nodes.title: ACQUIRED (Aplastic Anemia)
nodes.body:
• Aplastic Anemia:
    • Radiation (ex. Cancer chemo Survivors) - Toxins
    • Pregnancy, Infections (Hepatitis - non A/B/C)
    • Idiopathic (most common)

nodes.title: Dyskeratosis Congenita
nodes.body: • PEx: Oral leukoplakia, nail dystrophy, skin hyperpigmentation ("lacy" on neck + back)

nodes.title: Drugs
nodes.body:
• Folate Antagonists (Methotrexate)
  • Chemotherapy Drugs that alter DNA synthesis (ex. HYDROXYUREA)

nodes.title: Vitamin B12 Deficiency
nodes.body:
• DDx: ↑ Homocysteine, ↓ Methionine, ↑ Propionyl-CoA, ↓ Succinyl CoA, ↓Serum B12
    • Specific: ↑MMA (Normal in B9 Deficiency), Anti-Intrinsic factor antibodies.
  • PEx: ↓dTMP - Megalob. MACROCYTIC ANEMIA
    • ↑MMA - NEUROLOGIC symptoms ex. PERIPHERAL NEUROPATHY)
    • ↑ 5Methyl THF - if Vit B12 def anemia is treated with folate (symptoms masked)
      • → PERMANENT Neurologic Damage
  • Etiology:
    • Diet ("TEA and TOAST" or VEGANS)
    • PERNICIOUS ANEMIA (Abs to IF)
    • Gastrectomy, Ileal resection, IBD.
    • Pregnancy (↑ demand)
    • Pancreatic Insufficiency
  • Tx: SUPPLEMENTATION: Cobalamin Intramuscular INJECTIONS (or ↑ dose if ORAL)
    • (Hematologic response is rapid, but neurological improvement is slow)
    • ↳ Treat underlying cause.

nodes.title: Cobalamin (Vitamin B12)
nodes.body:
• Ⓐ Methionine synthesis
  • Ⓑ Succinyl CoA Synthesis.
  • Ⓒ 5 Methyl THF Recycling
  • Source: Exclusively made by BACTERIA ∴ ANIMAL products only.
  • Absorption: STOMACH and ILEUM, needs (IF) INTRINSIC FACTOR (Gastric Parietal Cells), R-protein, and protease from PANCREAS.
  • Stored: Liver stores 3-5 YEARS worth (Deficiency is usually CHRONIC in nature)

nodes.body:
• When should you avoid platelet transfusions?
  • Which conditions present w. ↓ platelets and schistocytes?
  • Why do we need to bridge warfarin therapy w. heparin initially?
  • How would you reverse warfarin in bleeding emergency?
  • What is transfused during massive transfusion protocol?

notes.name: Approach to a Bleeding Patient and Transfusion

nodes.title: Liver
nodes.body:
• 1° → Synthesize THROMBOPOIETIN ⊕ → BONE MARROW (THROMBOPOIESIS)
  • 2° →
    • FIBRINOGEN (Factor I)
    • PLASMINOGEN
    • VITAMIN K-dependant clotting factors: II, VII, IX, X, Protein C and S

nodes.title: Bone Marrow
nodes.body:
• THROMBOPOIESIS
    • Megakaryocytes

nodes.title: 2° Hemostasis (Fibrin Clot)
nodes.body: • ← Clotting factors V, VIII, XI, XIII, VWF, PLs, Ca²⁺ from PLATELETS

nodes.title: Coagulation Cascade
nodes.body:
• Intrinsic Pathway: (12, 11, 9, 8) (INSIDE), "Playing Table Tennis", Monitored via PTT
    • Activating surface (-ve charged PL surface of activated platelets) → XII → XIIa
    • (Factor XII not essential IN VIVO, does NOT confer ↑bleeding risk if deficient)
    • XIIa → Kallikrein; HMWK → Bradykinin; ACE ⊣ Bradykinin
    • XIIa: XI → XIa → (Ca²⁺) IX → IXa
    • VIII (bound to vWF) → FVIIIa, Ca²⁺, PL: Hemophilia A, Von Willebrand Disease
    • IXa + FVIIIa → X → Xa
  • Extrinsic Pathway: (7 + 3) (OUTSIDE), "Playing Tennis", Monitored via PT and INR
    • Trauma → TF; Release TISSUE FACTOR (coag. factor III) "INITIATION" (← Release TF from endothelium)
    • TF (VIIa, Ca²⁺, PL): VII → VIIa; ⊖ TFPI
    • VIIa (Ca²⁺, PL) → X → Xa
  • Common Pathway: (5 x 2 x 1) and 13...
    • Xa (+ FVa, Ca²⁺, PL): Prothrombin II → Thrombin IIa
    • Apixaban, Rivaroxaban, Edoxaban ⊣ Xa
    • Thrombin: +ve feedback: activates V, VIII, X, XIII "AMPLIFICATION"
    • Thrombin ⊣ ⊖ DIRECT INHIBITORS: ARGATROBAN, DABIGATRAN; INDIRECT INHIBITOR (VIA VITAMIN K): WARFARIN
    • Fibrinogen I → Fibrin formation Ia → Fibrin Mesh formation
    • XIIIa: "CLOT STABILIZATION": Crosslinking of fibrin strands
    • XIII is NOT measured by PT, INR or PTT
    • Fibrinogen activity monitored via TT or FIBRINOGEN levels
  • Protein C, S (↓ VIIIa, Va)

nodes.title: PTT ↑ DDx
nodes.body:
• HEPARIN (unfraction.)
  • HEMOPHILIA
  • Lupus Anticoagulant
  • Severe VWDisease, DIC
  • Single Factor 12, 11, 9, 8 ↓

nodes.title: INR/PT ↑ DDx
nodes.body:
• WARFARIN
  • Liver Disease
  • Vitamin K defic.
  • Factor VII defic.
  • DIC

nodes.title: Factor VIII Bound to vWF
nodes.body:
• in circulation: when VWF binds to SEC then FVIII is released
  • VIII → VIIIa via THROMBIN (IIa)

notes.name: Approach to a Bleeding Patient and Transfusion

nodes.title: Antithrombin III
nodes.body:
• ⊣ Xa, ⊣ Thrombin (IIa)
  • (Also ↓ IXa, XIa, XIIa)

nodes.title: Mixing Study
nodes.body:
• PT and PTT can be followed by MIXING STUDY
  • Normalize PT or PTT: CLOTTING FACTOR DEFICIENCY ex. Hemophilia
  • Does NOT Normalize PT or PTT: FACTOR INHIBITOR → ex. Lupus Anticoagulant

nodes.title: Lupus Anticoagulant
nodes.body:
• Classically seen in ANTIPHOSPHOLIPID ANTIBODY SYNDROME, Prevents PLs from activating coag. cascade: Falsely ↑PTT INVITRO but IN VIVO it's actually PRO-THROMBOTIC
  • (See THROMBOPHILIAS below)

nodes.title: Anticoagulants
nodes.body:
• (INHIBITORS OF 2° HEMOSTASIS)
  • PROTEIN C, S, ANTITHROMBIN III, TFPI
  • ↓ Clotting factors but do NOT break up existing clots (i.e. NOT FIBRINOLYTIC)

nodes.title: 3° Hemostasis: Fibrinolysis
nodes.body:
• Stimulated by tPA (TISSUE PLASMINOGEN ACTIVATOR)
  • Inhibited by PAI-1, TAFI
  • HYPERFIBRINOLYSIS control via tranexamic acid
  • Plasminogen → (tPA) → Plasmin → Fibrin Degradation Products (D-dimer)
    • TRANEXAMIC ACID (Reversal of tPA) ⊣ Plasminogen
    • PAI-1 (Plasminogen Activator Inhibitor) ⊖ tPA
    • TAFI (Fibrinolysis Inhibitor) ⊖ Fibrin Degradation Products

nodes.title: PT and Factor VII
nodes.body:
• Shortest half life of coag. factors: ↓ in liver disease, use of WARFARIN and vitamin K deficiency, monitored w. PT.
    • ↳ if liver disease is SEVERE, factors II, X and IX will also ↓ and thus PT AND PTT will both ↑.

nodes.title: ↑d-Dimer
nodes.body:
• Helps to exclude diseases if -ve.
  • DVT, PE, DIC
  • Indicates presence of BLOOD CLOTS! (Thrombosis)

nodes.title: Fibrinolytic Disorders
nodes.body:
• ← 3°: Normal INR, PT and PTT, Normal platelets
  • DELAYED ONSET bleeding.
    • ↳ PAI-1 deficiency
    • FXIII deficiency
    • α2 antiplasmin deficiency
    • Hyperfibrinolysis

nodes.title: Liver and Vitamin-K Dependent Factors
nodes.body:
• "(10) 1972"
  • Liver: II, X, VII, IX, Protein C, S (γ-glutamyl carboxylase)
  • Oxidized Vitamin K → Epoxide Reductase → Reduced Vitamin K
    • ⊖ WARFARIN (on Epoxide Reductase)
  • Dietary or Synthesized by DISTAL BOWEL MICROORGANISMS

nodes.title: Coagulation Disorders (2° Hemostasis)
nodes.body:
• ← 2°: Abnormal INR, PT and/or PTT + JOINT/SOFT TISSUE BLEEDING
  • Hematoma, hemarthroses, ICH
    • ↳ onset is often less immediate than in platelet disorders

nodes.title: Fibrinogen
nodes.body:
• (FACTOR I)
  • Dysfunction or Deficiency

nodes.title: Multiple Factor Deficiencies
nodes.body:
• → ↑dose Heparin and NOVEL ORAL ANTICOAGS.
  • → DIC (see platelet disorders)
  • Severe Disease → Liver, Vitamin K and Warfarin

nodes.title: Isolated ↑INR or PT Extrinsic Pathway
nodes.body:
• → Hereditary Factor VII deficiency/Inhibitor
  • Moderate Disease → Liver, Vitamin K and Warfarin

nodes.title: Isolated ↑PTT: Intrinsic Pathway
nodes.body:
• → UNFRACTIONATED HEPARIN
  • PTT does NOT Correct with mixing study → Factor Inhibition
  • PTT corrects with MIXING STUDY → Factor Deficiencies

nodes.title: Factor Inhibition
nodes.body:
• PTT does NOT Correct with mixing study
  • Non-specific → LUPUS ANTICOAGULANT
  • Specific factor inhibitor:
    • Factor VIII → Acquired Hemophilia A
    • Factor IX → ACQUIRED HEMOPHILIA B

nodes.title: Acquired Hemophilia a
nodes.body:
• PATH: Autoantibody to FVIII
  • PEx: SUDDEN Bleeding, more common in older adults.
  • PHx: Malignancy, autoimmune disorders ex. Lupus.
  • Tx: Manage bleed. Treat underlying disease. Immunosuppress: Glucocorticoids, Rituximab.
  • Acquired: More common in ADULTS; Hereditary: More common in CHILDREN

notes.name: Approach to a Bleeding Patient and Transfusion

nodes.title: Factor Deficiencies
nodes.body:
• PTT corrects with MIXING STUDY
  • FACTOR IX → Hereditary Hemophilia B
  • FACTOR VIII → Hereditary Hemophilia A; → Von Willebrand Disease

nodes.title: Hereditary Hemophilia B
nodes.body:
• (1 in 30,000)
  • X-LINKED: MALES affected, female carriers may be symptomatic
  • SUDDEN bleeding, with other typical features of coag. disorders.
  • Acquired: More common in ADULTS; Hereditary: More common in CHILDREN

nodes.title: Hereditary Hemophilia a
nodes.body:
• (1 in 5,000)
  • X-LINKED: MALES affected, female carriers may be symptomatic
  • SUDDEN bleeding, with other typical features of coag. disorders.
  • Acquired: More common in ADULTS; Hereditary: More common in CHILDREN

nodes.title: Neonates' Liver
nodes.body:
• Maturation 0-6 m.o
  • ↓ coag. factors (except FVIII and VWF)
  • ↑ PT and PTT

nodes.title: Vitamin K Deficiency
nodes.body:
• ∴ Vitamin ADEK: stored in fat,
    • ∴ Vit K deficiency is usually CHRONIC
  • Malabsorption ex. CYSTIC FIBROSIS
  • ↓ F II, VII, IX, X, protein C and S. ↑INR/PT.
  • Does not directly affect bleeding time or platelets
  • Compounds → Hemorrhagic Disease of Newborn

nodes.title: Hemorrhagic Disease of Newborn
nodes.body:
• Early HDN (1st day of life): Maternal meds (ex. anti-epileptics)
  • Classic HDN (2-7 d.o): exclusively in breastfed infants (↓vitamin K in breastmilk)
  • Late HDN (1wk-6 mo): due to Vitamin K malabsorption.

nodes.title: Liver, Vitamin K and Warfarin
nodes.body: • Severe Disease / Moderate Disease

nodes.title: Liver Disease
nodes.body:
• ↓ F II, VII, IX, X protein C and S
  • Normal FVIII, ↑INR/PT.
  • ↓ TPO = ↓ platelet production ∴ THROMBOCYTOPENIA and ↑ bleeding time
  • + many other signs of liver disease...
  • (From Week 10 Quiz) * DIC vs. Liver Disease:
    • Factor VIII: ↓ in DIC, ↑ in Liver Disease (Released by Endoth.)

nodes.title: Vitamin K Inhibitors: Warfarin
nodes.body:
• Inhibits Vitamin K Epoxide Reductase: ANTICOAGULANT
  • ↓ II, VII, IX, X, C, S
    • ↳ ↓THROMBIN main reason for anticoag. effect.
  • Long-half life (vs. Heparin)
  • (RECALL week 8 FoM: CYP2C9 variability)

nodes.title: Starting Warfarin
nodes.body: • PROTEIN C has shortest half-life of all vit-K dependant products. When protein C ↓ there is a transient HYPERCOAGULABLE STATE (worsens condition): Need to BRIDGE w. HEPARIN

nodes.title: Monitoring Warfarin
nodes.body:
• Monitor via INR/PT, if these ↑↑ then ↓ dose accordingly.
    • ↳ INR TARGET: 2.0-3.0! for VTE, Peripheral Arterial Disease or Atrial Fib, aortic valve prosthesis:
  • WARFARIN is GOLD STANDARD for MECHANICAL HEART VALVES
  • Note: TERATOGENIC (crosses placenta)
  • Adverse Effect: BLEEDING

nodes.title: Reversing Warfarin
nodes.body:
• (due to bleeding)
  • Vitamin K (← ensures there's no rebound coagulopathy once PCC wears off.)
  • PROTHROMBIN COMPLEX CONCENTRATE (Octaplex, Beriplex)
  • Fresh Frozen Plasma.

nodes.title: Antiphospholipid Antibody Syndrome
nodes.body:
• LUPUS ANTICOAGULANT (LAC)*: IN VITRO it falsely ↑PTT (typical of bleeding disorders)
  • Can measure antiphospholipid antibody **
  • ↑RR for VTEs (80x)
  • Cannot measure LAC or ATIII while on LMWH

nodes.title: Thrombophilia
nodes.body:
• → ACQUIRED → Antiphospholipid Antibody Syndrome
  • ↳ SCREENING INDICATIONS:
    • Idiopathic DVT/PE - young, recurrent, Family Hx, unusual location of VTEs.
    • Recurrent PREGNANCY LOSS.
  • Increases RELATIVE RISK (RR) of VTEs.

nodes.title: Thrombosis: Hypercoagulation and Clotting Disorders
nodes.body:
• → POLYCYTHEMIA VERA & ESSENTIAL THROMBOCYTHEMIA (Week 11 FoM)
  • TREATMENT → Anticoagulation Medication; ⊕ ANCILLARY treatment ex. NSAIDS, limb elevation

nodes.title: Anticoagulation Medication
nodes.body: • For VTE treatment/prophylaxis, atrial fibrillation stroke prevention, mechanical heart valves, arterial throm.

nodes.title: Direct Oral Anticoagulants (DOACs)
nodes.body:
• (Do not rely on AT-III)
  • Expensive, predictable PKs, wide Ther. windows, fixed dose, NO MONITORING
  • Renal Elimination (except Argatroban)

nodes.title: Direct Xa Inhibitors
nodes.body:
• APIXABAN, RIVAROXABAN, and EDOXABAN (The "XA" drugs)
  • Use: Anticoag, DVT prophylaxis
  • Reversal: ANDEXANET-A, or PCC in emergency bleeding.

nodes.title: Direct Thrombin (IIa) Inhibitors
nodes.body:
• ARGATROBAN, DABIGATRAN
  • Safe for RENAL FAILURE (Liver clearance)
  • Consider in HEPARIN INDUCED THROMBOCYTOPENIA (HIT) and ATIII deficiency (renal impairment)
  • Dabigatran Reversal: IDARUCIZUMAB
  • DIRECT THROMBIN INHIBITORS: UNIVALENT (Argatroban, Dabigatran); BIVALENT → Hirudin

nodes.title: Direct IV Thrombin Inhibitors
nodes.body:
• Special situation:
  • (do not rely on activity of AT-III)

nodes.title: Hirudin
nodes.body:
• BIVALENT direct thrombin inhibitor
  • DERIVATIVES: LEPIRUDIN, DESIRUDIN
  • ANALOGUE: BIVALIRUDIN
  • Can inactivate fibrin-bound thrombin (vs. Heparin which can only bind free thrombin)
  • Limitation: IMMUNOGENIC (anaphylactic risk in re-exposure)

nodes.title: Heparin
nodes.body:
• Potentiates ANTITHROMBIN
  • Does NOT cross PLACENTA: Safe to use in PREGNANCY (vs. Warfarin is Teratogenic)
  • Monitor with aPTT (PTT should ↑) for UFH.
  • Adverse Events: Bleeding, osteoporosis, HIT (see platelet disorders)
  • Contraindicated: active bleeding, recent CNS surgery, thrombocytopenia.

nodes.title: Unfractionated Heparin: UFH
nodes.body:
• (IV Continuous Infusion)
  • Variable size, activity and PK
  • Pentasaccharide chain in 30%:
    • <18 saccharides: inhibit Xa only
    • >18 saccharides: inhibit Xa + IIa
    • via ANTI-THROMBIN-III
  • SHORT HALF LIFE → Con: x3/day dose, Needs REGULAR PTT MONITORING!
  • Pro: easy to REVERSE: Reversed w. PROTAMINE SULFATE
  • Degraded in the liver by RES: SAFE FOR RENAL FAILURE Patients (acute or chronic)
    • ↳ NOTE: Anticoagulant of choice for patients w. RENAL FAILURE is WARFARIN!

nodes.title: Low Molecular Weight Heparin: LMWH
nodes.body:
• (Subcutaneous - SC injection)
  • (ex. Enoxaparin: Lovenox) or DALTEPARIN (used in VTE prophylaxis)
  • ↑ ability to inactivate Xa, ↓ ability to inactivate IIa.
  • ↑ BIOAVAILABILITY, Long T½
  • Predictable PKs: Does NOT need MONITORING
    • ↳ Does NOT affect PTT, if must monitor - use anti-Xa levels directly instead.
  • RENAL CLEARANCE: Half life prolonged in RENAL FAILURE
  • Long-term anticoag. of choice for CANCER patients.

nodes.title: Synthetic Heparin: Fondaparinux
nodes.body:
• (Subcutaneous)
  • Only inhibits Xa (indirectly)
    • ↳ higher affinity to AT-III
  • Monitoring not necessary
  • Eliminated in unchanged form via urine.

nodes.title: HIT: Heparin Induced Thrombocytopenia
nodes.body: • (see 1° hemostasis disorders)

nodes.title: Venous Thromboembolism
nodes.body:
• PREDISPOSING FACTORS (Virchow's Triad): Stasis, injury and hypercoagulability (ex. thrombophilia)
  • CLOTS in proximal deep veins of legs (POPLITEAL or higher)
  • Most are NOT preventable (spontaneous), 30% in CANCER patients.
  • Highest risk: Hip fracture or joint arthroplasty.
    • ↳ Prevention: Early mobilization and anticoagulants. PROPHYLAXIS should be considered in any person admitted to hospital.

nodes.title: DVT or PE Treatment
nodes.body:
• 1. 5-7 days: LMWH (SC)
  • 2. WARFARIN or DOACs:
  • DURATION varies: 3 months (low-risk), 6 months (mod-risk), LIFELONG (high-risk):
    • CANCER PATIENTS: Minimum of 6 months. If cancer cured Tx can stop. If still on chemo past 6 months switch to DOACs if on LMWH. Can stop if no cure.
    • Patients w. major transient risk factor (ex. TRAUMA): 3 months.
    • Patients w. IDIOPATHIC DVT or PE:
      • Men: Stay on Tx lifelong.
      • Women: Depends on predictors: Age >65, BMI >30, D-Dimer >250, Signs of "POST-THROMBOTIC SYNDROME"
        • 2 or more: Stay on Tx indef.
        • 1 or less: Stop at 6 months
        • Note: "DO NOT STOP OCPs" (Not evidence-based)
    • ↳ Investigate possible thrombophilia or cancer.
  • GOAL: Prevent death due to PE!
  • If >30% RISK of [?VTE] RECURRENCE: ANTICOAGULANTS used LIFELONG!

nodes.title: Platelets
nodes.body:
• Organelle Zone: Granules
    • ALPHA: PAI-1, VWF, FIBRINOGEN, clotting Factors (V, VIII, XI, XIII), HMWK
    • DELTA: ADP, Ca2+, histamine, serotonin, epineph.
  • Peripheral Zone: GPs, PLs (source of TXA2), open canalicular system.
  • Sol-Gel Zone: cytoskeleton
  • Membrane System: Ca2+ stores, enzymes.
  • VWF initiates Adhesion → 1° HEMOSTASIS

notes.name: Approach to a Bleeding Patient and Transfusion

nodes.title: Spleen
nodes.body:
• Platelet storage (30%) and 70% in bloodstream. (Lifespan = 10 days)
  • Destroys opsonized platelets via RES

nodes.title: 1° Hemostasis (Platelet Plug)
nodes.body:
• Adhesion, Activation, Aggregation
  • Figure: vWF Releases FACTOR VIII!; α-granules: α- starts cascade!
  • Exposed Subendothelial Collagen (Exposed SEC)
  • ADAMTS13 Degrades VWF multimers (regulatory)

notes.name: Approach to a Bleeding Patient and Transfusion

nodes.title: Adhesion
nodes.body: • (platelet - SEC) via GpIbR-VWF

notes.name: Approach to a Bleeding Patient and Transfusion

nodes.title: ACTIVATION and contraction
nodes.body:
• Platelet releases ADP (binds GpIbR)
  • Arachidonic acid converted to THROMBOXANE A2 via CYCLOOXYGENASE → ↑Cytosolic CALCIUM, ↑platelet activation, VASOCONSTRICTION
  • COX → TXA2, ⊖ by ASPIRIN

notes.name: Approach to a Bleeding Patient and Transfusion

nodes.title: Aggregation
nodes.body:
• (platelet-platelet)
  • Crosslink via GpIIb/IIIaR and Fibrinogen
  • Ca2+ → GpIIb/IIIaR (translocation to cell surface)
  • GpIIb/IIIaR: Target for antibodies in ITP

notes.name: Approach to a Bleeding Patient and Transfusion

nodes.title: Endothelial Injury
nodes.body:
• ① Neural-mediated TRANSIENT (reflex) VASOCONSTRICTION
  • ② Exposed SEC
  • ③ Release TF

nodes.title: Antiplatelet Medication
nodes.body:
• Adverse effects (ex. bleeding)
  • ASPIRIN ⊖ COX
  • CLOPIDOGREL ⊖ P2Y12(ADP)R (can cause TTP)
  • ABCIXIMAB ⊖ GpIIb/IIIaR

notes.name: Approach to a Bleeding Patient and Transfusion

nodes.title: Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome (HUS)
nodes.body:
• PATH: Capillary microthrombosis due to SHIGA-like toxin from E. Coli (O157:H7) - ex Hamburgers.
  • Seen more commonly in children
  • PEx + DDx: Hematochezia, melena w. DIARRHEA, All lab findings listed below + normal ADAMTS13
  • Tx: Supportive (IV fluids), avoid antibiotics (may worsen disease)
  • AVOID PLATELET TRANSFUSION (would worsen condition)

nodes.title: Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura (TTP)
nodes.body:
• PATH: ↓ADAMTS13 (due to autoimmune, congenital, pregnancy) - ↑VWF multimers
    • ↑platelet adhesion + aggregation
  • Seen more commonly in adults
  • PEx + DDx: All listed below + ↓ADAMTS13, fever and NEUROLOGIC symptoms (↓brain perfusion, may be strokes).
  • Tx: PLASMA exchange, steroids → Rituximab (refractory)
  • AVOID PLATELET TRANSFUSION (would worsen condition)

nodes.title: Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia (HIT)
nodes.body:
• (THROMBOSIS (Not bleeding) disorder)
  • PATH: UFH (more common than LMWH) for >4 days → Heparin/Platelet F4 complex IgG antibodies → Platelet activation and consumption → ↓platelets + THROMBOSIS
  • DDx: Clinical suspicion based on 4T's SCORE: Thrombocytopenia, Timing of plt ↓, Thrombosis or other sequelae (ex skin necrosis), other causes for Thrombocytopenia: sensitive + NOT specific.
    • Confirm HIT via: PF4/Heparin EIA (enzyme immunoassay) - sensitive + NOT specific HIT test.
    • + Serotonin Release Assay: Sensitive AND specific.
  • Tx: STOP ALL HEPARIN (UFH, LMWH and flushes). Start alternative anticoagulant (ex. Argatroban). Start warfarin once platelets have normalized.
    • (AVOID PLATELET TRANSFUSION)

nodes.title: Thrombotic Microangiopathies
nodes.body:
• "MICROANGIOPATHIC HEMOLYTIC ANEMIAS" (MIHAs) - Excessive microthrombi causing:
    • Hemolytic Anemia (due to narrow lumen): ↓Hgb, ↓haptoglobin, ↑LDH, SCHISTOCYTES
    • Thrombocytopenia (due to ↑consumption): ↓platelets, ↑bleeding time.
    • Acute kidney injury (due to low perfusion): ↑Cr, ↓GFR.
  • Moderate 50-99 plt → HUS
  • Severe <10 plt → TTP

nodes.title: Immune Thrombocytopenic Purpura (ITP)
nodes.body:
• aka. Immune Thrombocytopenia.
  • PATH: Anti-GpIIb/IIIaR antibodies (Platelets destroyed at spleen, ↓prod'n.)
  • PEx + DDx: ↓platelets, ↑bleeding time
    • Normal PT/INR, PTT, D-dimer, LDH, CBC (diagnosis of exclusion)
  • PHx: Infection, SLE, malignancy - Hx of AUTOIMM.
  • Tx: GLUCOCORTICOIDS (Prednisone, dexamethasone) → IVIG → RITUXIMAB + TPO Mimetics, Immune suppression,
    • If ↓platelets persist: SPLENECTOMY (refractory)

nodes.title: Disorders due to Increased Destruction
nodes.body:
• Most are ACUTE (DIC can be acute or chronic)
  • → HIT: Mod-Severe
  • → ITP: Severe <10 plt
  • → DIC: Acute = Severe, Chronic = Moderate

nodes.title: Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC)
nodes.body:
• PATH: STRESSOR (Trauma, cancer, sepsis) leads to CONSUMPTIVE COAGULOPATHY: ↓anticoagulants, ↓Fibrinolysis, ↓platelets, ↓coagulation factors.
    • = Hypercoaguable state + bleeding → microvascular obstruction: Multi-organ ischemia and failure → Schistocytes
  • May present w. "oozing of blood from IVs", hemorrhages, DVT, PE, melena, hematuria.
  • DDx: ↓platelets, ↑bleeding time, ↑PT, ↑PTT, ↓FIBRINOGEN, ↑D-DIMER, ↑LDH, Schistocytes
    • "everything is over consumed"...
  • Tx: Treat underlying stressor, supportive (IV fluids, monitor), TRANSFUSIONS

nodes.body:
• Fibrinogen <1: CRYOPRECIPITATE
  • Platelets <50: PLATELETS
  • INR >1.5: FRESH FROZEN PLASMA
  • Hemoglobin <70-80: PACKED RBCs

nodes.title: Von Willebrand Disease
nodes.body:
• PATH: HEREDITARY mutation in VWF gene
    • Type 1: ↓VWF (AD) - 80% of cases
    • Type 2: ↓fn of VWF (AR) - most severe
    • Type 3: NO VWF (AD or AR)
    • → ↓platelet adhesion (1° hemostasis)
    • ↓FVIII binding to VWF = ↑FVIII destruction (2° hemostasis)
  • Test via: VWF antigen, VWF activity assay (RiCof), FVIII level, BLOOD GROUP (Group O patients have 30% less than non-O)
    • → Abnormal RISTOCETIN Test, Corrects w. mixed plasma. → SPECIALIZED TESTING
  • PEx and DDx: Normal platelet, ↑bleeding time, normal PT, ↑PTT, ↓VIII and VWF antigen, family history

nodes.title: Deep Vein Thrombosis (DVT)
nodes.body:
• S/S: Swelling (usually leg), erythema, warmth, pain
  • DIAGNOSIS: Cannot be made on clinical grounds alone.
    • (Pre-test probability of DVT predicted using standardized model)
    • presence of alternative diagnosis does NOT rule out DVT.
  • D-DIMER: Levels tested via ELISA. -ve test to EXCLUDE DVT. +ve test (↑D-DIMER) needs to be confirmed w. ultrasound.
  • COMPRESSION ULTRASOUND (may need to repeat in 5-7d, if so, patient should not be anticoagulated in the interim)
  • (ASCENDING VENOGRAM (invasive) no longer used to diagnose.) "gold standard"
  • Venous thrombus EMBOLIZED from DVT → PE

nodes.title: Pulmonary Embolism (PE)
nodes.body:
• S/S: Pleuritic chest pain, dyspnea, syncope, tachycardia, hemoptysis.
    • 50% of PE have no symptoms of DVT
  • DIAGNOSIS: Similar to DVT in that cannot be made based on clinical grounds alone. Unlike DVT, PE can be ruled out if alternative diagnosis made.
    • (Like DVT, Pre-test probability of PE also calculated w. standardized model)
  • D-DIMER: -ve test excludes PE, +ve test (↑[?DD]) is followed up with:
  • CTPA (CT PULMONARY ANGIOGRAM): 1st choice if past abnormal CXR or suspected lung cancer that can also be identified via CT.
    • OR
  • V/Q SCAN (V = Ventilation, Q = Perfusion): 1st choice for younger women (↓radiation) or renal failure patients. If V/Q is "non-diagnostic" follow up w.
    • → BILATERAL COMPRESSION ULTRASOUND. (or CTPA if -ve but PE is likely)
  • (PULMONARY ANGIOGRAM (invasive) no longer used to diagnose PE) "gold standard"

nodes.title: Polycythemia Vera (PV)
nodes.body:
• (↓EPO and all 3 cell lines ↑, RBCs ↑↑)
  • (ACQUIRED 1° ERYTHROCYTOSIS)
  • POLYCYTHEMIA = PANCYTOSIS aka. all 3 cell lines are elevated w. ↑↑RBCs.
  • DDx: ↑Hb, ↑HCT, ↑WBCs, ↑Plt, LOW EPO + one of:
    • JAKV617F +ve (in 90% of PV)
    • JAK2 Exon 12 mutation +ve
    • BMS: Hypercellularity of all 3 cell lines (including megakaryocytes)
  • PATH: JAK2 mutation (V617F) → ↑Kinase domain activity (w.o. EPO) at growth receptors: MYELOID PROLIFERATION → HYPERVISCOSITY → THROMBOSIS (A or V) and HYPERTENSION. (PEx related to HYPOXIA and HYPERCOAGULATION)
  • PEx: More common in older ADULTS, PLETHORA, mucosal cyanosis, aquagenic pruritis, erythromelalgia, digit ischemia, SPLENOMEGALY, neurologic symptoms (HA, visual, dizziness)
  • Tx: Goal is to ↓ HEMATOCRIT to <45%. ASPIRIN (ex. ECASA)
    • Low-risk of thrombosis: PHLEBOTOMY (↓Hb only)
    • High-risk of thrombosis: HYDROXYUREA (Cytoreduction ↓ all cell lines)
      • → if Age >60 or prior thrombosis.
    • Prognosis: 2-3 years no Tx, slight ↑ if Tx.

notes.name: Approach to Leukocytosis and Myeloproliferative Neoplasms

nodes.title: (ET) Essential Thrombocythemia (1°)
nodes.body:
• PATH: JAK2 mutation → ↑Tyrosine Kinase Act → MEGAKARYOCYTOSIS
  • DDx: Isolated ↑↑Plt (Normal RBCs, WBCs) - ↑risk of THROMBOSIS
    • BM Biopsy: MEGAKARYOCYTE HYPERPLASIA
    • PBS: Clusters of platelets
  • Tx: Low dose ASPIRIN and:
    • Low-risk of thrombosis: MONITOR only.
    • High-risk of thrombosis: HYDROXYUREA (cytoreduction)
      • → Age >60, prior thrombosis.
  • Prognosis: slight ↓ than normal if no Tx.

nodes.title: Chronic Myeloproliferative Neoplasms (MPNs)
nodes.body:
• More common in OLDER ADULTS (Age >60)
  • JAKV617F mutation in 90% of PV, 50% of ET and 1° MF.
    • → PV w. ↑RBCs, ET w. ↑Plt, 1° MF w. Pancytopenia
  • Other mutations: PV: JAK2 Exon 12, ET + MF: MPL, CALR genes
  • Common features: SPLENOMEGALY. Risk of transform into AML, mortality often due to THROMBOSIS, BLEEDING or → AML.
  • SPLENOMEGALY → EARLY SATIETY!!
  • Diagnostic criteria based on WHO 2016 classification.

nodes.body:

    • → MOA: Cytoreduction via ↓ DNA deoxyribonucleotides.
  • Tx for SICKLE CELL DISEASE
    • → MOA: ↑HbF, exact MOA not clear
  • One of various cytotoxic drugs that causes MEGALOBLASTIC ANEMIA

notes.name: Approach to Leukocytosis and Myeloproliferative Neoplasms

nodes.title: Myelofibrosis (MF)
nodes.body:
• PATH: JAK2, CALR or MPL mutation - Atypical Megakaryocytes → BM FIBROSIS, w. EXTRAMEDULLARY HEMATOPOIESIS
    • → ∴ Massive SPLENOMEGALY.
  • DDx: PANCYTOPENIA, but ↑Plt and ↑Neutrophils may be present.
    • PBS: TEAR DROP CELLS and LEUKOERYTHROBLASTIC PICTURE (Granulocyte LEFT SHIFT and nucleated RBCs)
    • BM Biopsy: RETICULIN strands, Atypical Megakaryocyte hyperplasia (early)
    • BM Aspiration: "DRY TAP", hypocellular, fibrosis.
  • Tx: Curative: Stem cell transplantation (if eligible)
    • Conventional: Transfusions, steroids, hydroxyurea, EPO.
    • Newer: Targeted-JAK Inhibitor (RUXOLITINIB)

nodes.title: Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (CML)
nodes.body:
• (↑↑ Neutrophils, ↑ Metamyelocytes)
  • PEx: More common in OLDER ADULTS. Chronic phase (yrs) w. mild symptoms. Accelerated phase: Anemia, infections, splenomegaly. If untreated → Blast crisis (resembles AML)
  • PATH: t(9;22) transloc → PHILADELPHIA Chromosome, BCR-ABL fusion → Tyrosine Kinase ↑ (Week 6 FoM) - 100% of CML.
    • → Karyotyping via FISH.
  • DDx: ↑Neutrophils (w. Neut. LEFT SHIFT) on CBC and PBS. Variable RBC and PLT. GRANULOCYTOSIS on BMS.
  • Tx: IMATINIB (Gleevec) - Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitor. (Targeted Therapy)
    • ± Hydroxyurea, stem cell transplants.

nodes.title: Progression of ET, PV and MF
nodes.body:
• ET and PV → MF → AML
  • ET → MF
  • ET → AML
  • MDS → AML

nodes.title: Myeloid Disorders
nodes.body:
• PBS: Leukoerythroblastic Picture
    • → Check both PBS and BMS for BLASTS since they may not always show in PBS.
  • → Chronic myeloid disorders: <10% Blasts, ↑ Mature myeloid cells (RBCs, Plt, WBCs)
  • → AML: >10% Blasts and immature Myeloid Cells

nodes.title: Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML)
nodes.body:
• PEx: More common in OLDER ADULTS. Resp or neuro distress (leukostasis), fatigue, infections, bleeding, GINGIVAL HYPERPLASIA.
  • DDx: ↑↑↑ WBC (↓Mature WBCs), ↓Hb, ↓Plt ± electrolyte abnormalities. PBS or BMS w. >10% MYELOBLASTS w. AUER RODS
  • Tx: Aggressive but SHORT (4-6 wks in hospital)
    • 1. Induction → CHEMOTHERAPY to get remission
    • 2. Consolidation → STEM CELL TRANSPLANT (some) to keep remission.
      • → Cytogenetics to determine risk:
        • Low-risk: Aggressive Chemo
        • High-risk: SC Transplant (if young), low-dose chemo (if old)
  • SIDE EFFECTS:
    • BM Toxicity: ↓ WBC (Need ANTIBIOTICS), ↓ RBC/Plt (Need TRANSFUSIONS)
    • Anthracycline: Cardiac Toxicity
    • Cytarabine: Rashes, cerebellar toxicity.
  • HIGH MORTALITY

nodes.title: Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL)
nodes.body:
• ← >10% Blasts and immature Lymphoid Cells
  • PEx: More common in CHILDREN. LYMPHADENOPATHY, NIGHT SWEATS, FEVER, UNEXPLAINED WEIGHT LOSS. Pain, hepatosplenomegaly.
  • DDx: ↑↑ Lymphoblasts (↓WBCs). Flow Cytometry to distinguish:
    • B-CELL ALL (80%): t(12;21), CD19⁺, CD20⁺
    • T-CELL ALL (20%): CD2-8⁺.
    • BCR-ABL ⊕ = Aggressive ALL.
  • Complications: SANCTUARY sites (CNS and TESTES)
  • Tx: Low Dose chemo but LONG (3 years)
    • Very CURABLE (90%) in CHILDREN vs. POOR PROGNOSIS in ADULTS!
    • Complicated chemo regimens. (multi-agent)
    • CNS via lumbar punctures (± radiation) (CNS RELAPSE most common recurrence source)
    • → Risk stratification (ex. NCI/Rome Criteria, Standard risk if age >1, <10 and WBC <50)
    • Blinatumomab: Targets CD19⁺ on ALL B-cells (engages T-cells) 28 day IV infusion.
      • → New toxicities: CNS and cytokine release syndrome.
    • Inotuzamab: CD22 directed Ab. (in 90% of ALL)

nodes.title: Acute Promyelocytic Leukemia (APL)
nodes.body:
• Subtype of AML (one of many AML disorders)
  • PATH: t(15;17); (PML-RARα Fusion) → Abnormal Retinoic acid receptor → Differentiation arrested at Promyelocyte.
  • APL Subtypes: Hypergranular (75%), Microgranular.
  • DDx: Confirm w. CYTOGENETICS. Suggestive:
    • PBS/BMS: Myeloblasts w. AUER RODS ↑↑, ↑ Promyelocytes.
    • Flow Cyt: HLA-DR Surface marker -ve.
  • PEx: Similar to other acute leukemias, except:
    • Complication: Prone to DIC (Early death - ICH) and abnormal ↑ in fibrinolysis → Bleeding.
    • Good long-term survival.
  • Tx: ATRA (All-trans RETINOIC ACID - Derivative of Vitamin A) and ARSENIC. Chemo for high-risk.

nodes.title: CML, AML (+APL), ALL, CLL: Leukemia
nodes.body:
• PEx: Progressive CYTOPENIAS, LEUKOSTASIS (ex. Stroke, confusion, H/A)
  • CBC/DIFF: Anemia, thrombocytopenia, neutropenia or neutrophilia, BLASTS.
  • DDx: BONE MARROW Aspirate and Core Biopsy:
    • Flow Cytometry
    • Cytogenetics (Karyotype)
    • Molecular Tests (Gene Analysis)
    • MORPHOLOGY: old FAB Classifications M3/M4/M5 indicates leukemia.
      • → New WHO Classifications used.
  • Etiology:
    • Radiation (Cancer Tx) and Chemo.
    • Chemicals (Benzene, Alkylating agents)
    • Hereditary (ex. Trisomy 21)
    • HEMATOLOGICAL Causes: MDS and Myeloproliferative Disorders (PV, ET, MF)

nodes.title: Leukemia Complications
nodes.body:
• Especially if BLASTS >10% (AML/ALL)
  • → Complications often seen on initial PATIENT PRESENTATION
    • If Leukemia grows in bone marrow: (Myelophthisis - Week 9 FoM)

nodes.title: DIC
nodes.body:

  • Associated w. APL within first 72 hours of diagnosis!! (URGENT: LETHAL if undiagnosed)
  • ↑PTT, ↑INR, ↓Fibrinogen tested in any patient w. new blasts to check for DIC
  • → If DIC suspected and new blasts on PBS: Assume APL and START ATRA + Arsenic Tx

nodes.title: Leukostasis
nodes.body:
• (Med. Emergency)
  • Commonly seen with AML and ALL: WBC >100
  • CML: WBC >250
  • CLL (RARE!) WBC >400
  • (AML/ALL and CML) Typical feature of ACUTE LEUKEMIAS!
  • ↑↑ BLASTS and ↓ Perfusion: ex. STROKE, or PULMONARY DISTRESS

nodes.title: Tumor Lysis Syndrome

  • (more common in HEMATOLOGICAL CANCERS and CANCER TREATMENTS)

nodes.title: Multiple Myeloma
nodes.body:
• More common in OLDER ADULTS
  • PATH: ≥10% PLASMA CELLS - ↑M PROTEIN (Abnormal Igs)
    • BM Infiltration (w. PANCYTOPENIA) - Anemia, bleeding, infections
    • ↑Monoclonal antibodies (nephron filtration) - ACUTE KIDNEY INJURY
    • ↑Inflamm. Cytokines - ↑osteoclast activity - Hypercalcemia, pain & FRACTURES.
      • (Fractures may compress nerves - neurological symptoms)
  • PEx: BONE PAIN and lower back pain most common, ± symptoms above.
  • DDx:
    • Blood Tests & CBC:
      • Calcium - Hypercalcemia*
      • Renal - ↑Creatinine*
      • Anemia - ↓Hb*
    • XR, CT, MRI: Bone Disease - Fractures, Lesions*
    • ↓Plt, ↓WBC (Neuts.)
    • LDH (if ↑ = Poor Prognosis)
    • Liver Function tests
    • Serum ↑Ig (Normal or M-Protein)
    • PBS: ROULEAUX FORMATION
    • 24hr urine-PROTEIN ELECTROPHORESIS:
      • Presence of a serum or urinary MONOCLONAL PROTEIN*
    • Bone Marrow BIOPSY (Morphology, Flow cytometry)
      • ≥10% Monoclonal Plasma cells in BM*
  • Prognosis: ISS risk stratification - levels of Albumin and/or β-2 microglobulin, FISH, LDH↑.
  • Tx: DARATUMUMAB (targets CD38 on MM cells), Bortezomib (Velcade) + Dexamethasone.
    • Tx Complication: Anemia (+ PRBC Transfusion, EPO), bone lesions (+ Biphosphonates)

nodes.title: Approach to Mediastinal Mass
nodes.body:
• Systemic effects (ex. B-Symptoms) or mass effects (ex. SVC OBSTRUCTION w. +ve PEMBERTON SIGN, or HORNER'S SYNDROME)
  • ANTERIOR:
    • Thymus (Thymoma)
    • Terrible lymphoma
    • Teratoma & Germ cell tumor
    • Thyroid tumor
    • Thoracic Aorta
    • → 5Ts.
  • MIDDLE:
    • Lymphadenopathy
    • Benign cystic tumor
    • Esophageal tumors
    • Vascular masses or enlargement (ex. Aortic Aneurysm in WIDENED Mediastinum)
  • POSTERIOR:
    • Neurogenic tumor
    • Meningoceles
    • Thoracic spine lesion
  • Commonly presents w. lymphadenopathy - BIOPSY (Percutaneous, endobronchial, surgical)

nodes.title: Lymphadenopathy
nodes.body:
• Isolated, localized or generalized.
  • Generalized: Neoplastic (ex. hematological or metastatic), Drugs, Infectious (ex. Strep, Hep), Inflammatory (ex. RA, SLE)
  • PEx: location, size, character + associations (ex. fever, rash, mouth ulcers, SPLENOMEGALY, breast exam)
  • DDx:
    • TONSILS, CERVICAL (ANT & POST): more indicative of INFECTIONS
    • SUPRACLAVICULAR, INFRACLAVICULAR, AXILLARY, INGUINAL: more indicative of MALIGNANCY (especially if UNILATERAL)
    • → Signs of MALIGNANCY: Generalized, Fixed, NON-TENDER, Supraclavicular, PERSISTENT, rubbery, or firm (if met. solid tumor)
  • Hx Guides investigations and determine risk of malignancy:
    • High-risk: EXCISIONAL or CORE BIOPSY (NOT FNA) to diagnose LYMPHOMA - need ARCHITECTURE)
    • Low-risk + generalized: CBC/D + specific testing
    • Low-risk + regional: observe, biopsy if persistent.

nodes.title: B-Cell CLL
nodes.body:
• (30% of all leucemias)
  • PEx: More common in OLDER ADULTS. Asymptomatic in EARLY stage.
    • Late: Lymphadenopathy, fever, night sweats, unexplained weight loss, anemia, bleeding, infections (impaired BM)
    • → LEUKOSTASIS RARE w. CLL
  • PATH: Mutations → ↑Leukemic B cell proliferation, impaired differentiation
    • → ↑dysfunctional leukemic cells (B and T)
    • HYPOGAMMAGLOBULINEMIA (IgG, A, M ↓)
    • → Causes AUTOIMMUNE HEMOLYTIC ANEMIA (Hot or Cold AIHA)
  • DDx: PBS: ↑↑Lymphocytes, ↓granulocytes, ↓Hb, ↓platelets, ± Hemolysis labs.
    • SMUDGE CELLS
    • BMS: ↑mature lymphocytes
    • Flow Cytometry: CD19, 5, 23, 20.
    • Molecular Studies: P53 mutation, IgH variable reg.
  • RAI CLASSIFICATION SYSTEM: Stage 0-IV
    • → + doubling time, cytogenetics, mutated IgH variable gene = PROGNOSTIC Factors.
  • Tx: SLOW GROWING disease ∴ chemo less suitable.
    • DO NOT TREAT: Incurable or low-risk CLL.
    • TREAT IF: Cytopenias, ↑lymphaden, AIHA, ITP, B Symptoms.
    • → RITUXIMAB (Anti CD20)
    • IBRUTINIB (Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitor: B-Cell Recept. ↓)
    • Chemotherapy

nodes.title: Lymphoma
nodes.body:
• (NHL more common)
  • Approach: Hx, PEx, Staging, DDx work-up
  • PEx: B-SYMPTOMS: Weight loss, fever, NIGHT SWEATS, (aka. Constitutional symptoms), Non-specific symptoms of cancer (low energy, poor appetite, fatigue) and LYMPHADENOPATHY (if present check for SPLENOMEGALY)
  • DDx: Blood tests - CBC, chem, LDH (if ↑ = POOR PROGNOSIS), HBV, HCV, HIV.
    • Imaging: PET+CT SCAN (ultrasound first if pediatric) for STAGING of lymph nodes that are NOT PALPABLE on PEx.
    • Bone Marrow or Lymph Node BIOPSY (EXCISIONAL or CORE)
      • → FLOW CYTOMETRY:
        • Neoplastic B-lymphocytes are MONOCLONAL (only one light chain - Kappa or lamda), have aberrant CD EXPRESSION (T-cell CDs on B-cells) or may lose original CDs.

nodes.title: Ann Arbor Lymphoma Staging
nodes.body:
• Diagram: stages I, II, III, IV on body figures, with DIAPHRAGM line
  • STAGE I, II, III, IV and
    • → A: No B-Symptoms
    • → B: One or more B-symptoms.
    • → Others: E (Extension) or X (Bulky, >10cm)
  • → IV: BONE MARROW or extranodal sites, (excluding SPLEEN)
    • Need BM BIOPSY to stage this.

nodes.title: Non-Hodgkin's Lymphoma
nodes.body: • (>30 subtypes)

nodes.title: B-Cell (NH) Lymphoma
nodes.body:
• (more common than T-cell)
  • Composed of neoplastic monoclonal B-cells
  • AGRESSIVE NHL (usually curable) → DIFFUSE LARGE B-CELL LYMPHOMA
  • INDOLENT NHL (usually incurable) → FOLLICULAR LYMPHOMA

nodes.title: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma
nodes.body:
• Can affect patients of ALL AGES, Aggressive NHL
  • (Most common type of NHL)
  • PEx: Lymphadenopathy, B-symptoms.
  • Prognosis: IPI Scale (A.P.L.E.S. Risk factors)
  • Tx: Aim is CURE. Sensitive to chemotherapy.
    • CHOP-R (+ radiation if stage I/II)

nodes.title: Follicular Lymphoma
nodes.body:
• More common in OLDER ADULTS, INDOLENT - SLOW growing NHL
  • (Originating from GERMINAL CENTER)
  • PEx: Lymphadenopathy, SPLENOMEGALY, often ASYMPTOMATIC
  • Prognosis: FLIPI Scale (No. L.A.S.H Risk factors)
  • Tx: Aim is palliative (NOT curable unless stage I)
    • Stage I: RT alone
    • Stage II-IVA: Observation
    • Stage II-IVB: BR chemo + Rituximab (2 yrs)
    • (usually stage III/IV at diagnosis)

nodes.title: Classical Hodgkin's Lymphoma
nodes.body:
• (more common than non-class. HL)
  • NODULAR SCLEROSIS HL
  • MIXED CELLULARITY HL
  • LYMPHOCYTE RICH HL
  • LYMPHOCYTE DEPLETE HL

nodes.title: (Classical) Hodgkin's Lymphoma
nodes.body:
• (5 main subtypes)
  • Most common in YOUNG ADULTS.
  • PATH: Neoplastic RS cells (B-cell origin) - ↑INFLAMMATORY signals - ↑activation of reactive B-lymphocytes (non-neoplastic) in NODES.
  • DDx: NOT detected via Flow Cytometry, need LYMPH NODE BIOPSY:
    • (Neoplastic) REED-STERNBERG CELLS (Owl's eye, Binucleate)
    • → RS cells are negative for CD20 and CD45 (lost B-cell markers) but positive for CD15 and CD30 ∴ NORMAL FLOW CYTOMETRY (NO MONOCLONAL PATTERN or specific cytogenetic abnormality)
  • PEx: Lymphadenopathy w. CONTIGUOUS NODAL SPREAD ± B-symptoms. PRURITIS, lymph node pain w. ALCOHOL, MEDIASTINAL MASS.
  • Stage I/II Prognosis: ↑ESR, large mediastinal mass, ≥3 nodal regions, extranodal: FAVOURABLE if none of these factors
  • Stage III/IV Prognosis: 7 poor prognosis factors.
    • Guides Tx
  • Tx: similar Tx for 5 subtypes. All types of lymphoma are treatable.
    • ABVD chemo + RADIATION Therapy (# of cycles per prognosis).
    • → ex. NIVOLUMUMAB
    • Aim is to CURE (Most are curable)
    • (NOT TREATED w. RITUXIMAB - cells lose B-cell markers)
  • → Less common subtype: NON-CLASSICAL HODGKIN'S LYMPHOMA

nodes.title: Chemo Side Effects
nodes.body:
• Agent-specific:
    • ↑toxicity if agents from same MOA overlapped:
    • ↑acoustic damage and nephrotoxicity if both cyclophosphamide + cisplatin
    • → (pasted diagram, no heading): face is puffy from decadron; C for Cisplatin / Carboplatin: nephrotoxic & acoustic n. damage; V for Vincristine: peripheral neuropathy; D for Doxorubicin: cardiotoxic; B for Bleomycin: pulmonary fibrosis; Cy for Cyclophosphamide: hemorrhagic cystitis; M for MTX, 5 for 5FU & 6 for 6-MP: myelosuppression
  • vs. Common to all classic chemo:
    • BM SUPPRESSION: Anemia, Bleeding, Infections (may need transfusions)
    • DNA DAMAGE: ↑risk of new cancer, Chem-Leukemia, Lymphoma or solid cancer)
    • MUCOSITIS & ALOPECIA
    • FERTILITY Issues.

nodes.title: Hormonal Therapies
nodes.body:
• Glucocorticoids / Steroids
  • PREDNISONE and DEXAMETHASONE
  • MOA: ↓COX2 and Lipocortin - ↓Arachidonic Acid - ↓Prostaglandins & TXA2
  • ANTI-INFLAMMATORY - Treat autoimmun. disor.
  • TUMORICIDAL (Cytotoxic to LYMPHOCYTES)
    • → Treat Lymphoma, Lymphocytic Leukemia, Multiple myeloma

nodes.title: Monoclonal Antibodies
nodes.body:
• "__ mab"
  • NAKED → RITUXIMAB, DARATUMUMAB
  • CONJUGATED → ZEVALIN/ BEXAAR

nodes.title: Rituximab
nodes.body:
• NAKED
  • MOA: Targets CD20 on B-cells - killed via comp., NK lysis, or phagocytosis.
  • B-cell malig: CLL, ALL, DLBCL
  • RA, ITP, TTP, AIHA.
  • Combin. Therapy: CHOP-R

nodes.title: Daratumumab
nodes.body:
• NAKED
  • MOA: Targets CD38 on MULTIPLE MYELOMA cell
    • CD38 is also receptor, if ⊣ it ↓Adenosine in tumor environment (↓ATP)

nodes.title: Zevalin/ Bexaar
nodes.body:
• CONJUGATED: MAb conjugated to radiotherapy isotope or other drugs
  • → Treat some FOLLICULAR LYMPHOMA

nodes.title: Chop-R
nodes.body:
• Chemo Regimen:
  • For most B-CELL LYMPHOMAS (5 day cycle every 21 days)
    • Cyclophosphamide (IV-1)
    • Hydroxy-Doxorubicin. (IV-1)
    • Oncovin (Vincristine) (IV-1)
    • Prednisone (Oral 1-5)
    • Rituximab. (IV-1-5)
  • Other Lymphomas → RADIATION THERAPY

nodes.title: Radiation Therapy
nodes.body:
• Chemo + RADIATION commonly used in stage I/II lymphomas (Surgery not common in lymphoma management)
    • → Observation common for treatable but not curable disorders that grow slowly.
  • External Beam Radiation (EBRT) or BRACHYTHERAPY (Internally w. decaying radioactive isotopes near tumor)
  • Ionizing radiation damages DNA (via. e- directly or free radicals), doses are divided - FRACTIONATION → FOUR R's OF RADIOLOGY
    • (cancer cells do not repair themselves as effectively as normal cells - lethal vs. sublethal damage)
    • Fractionation spares normal cells via: REPAIR, REPOPULATION
    • Fractionation damages tumor cells via: REDISTRIBUTION, REOXYGENATION
  • Subacute Radiation toxicity: Myelosupression, radiation pneumonitis, radiation pericarditis, L'Hermitte's sign, fatigue.
  • Late Toxicity: Hypothyroidism, Herpes Zoster, Infertility, 2° cancer.
  • Modern Radiation:
    • Intensity modulated external beam radiation (IMRT)
    • Stereotactic Ablative Body Radiation (SABR) & Radiosurgery (SRS)

notes.name: Radiation Oncology, Quality Improvement and Critical Appraisal

nodes.title: CAR-T Cells
nodes.body:
• MOA: Chimeric Antigen Receptor gene inserted to pt's T-cells (in lab)
    • → Tx for RELASED ALL and DLBCL (if eligible - very expensive)

nodes.title: PD-1 & PDL-1 Inhibitors
nodes.body:
• PEMBROLIZUMAB (Keytruda)
  • NIVOLUMUMAB
  • MOA: Enhance T-cell recognition of tumor cells by preventing binding of PD-1 (T cell) to PDL-1 (tumor cell)
  • Side Effects: Autoimmune rxn's (treat w. steroids)
  • Tx for HODGKIN'S LYMPHOMA

nodes.title: Small Molecule Drugs
nodes.body: • → Others: PROTEOSOME INHIBITORS, Immunomodulatory Agents, Differentiating Agents

nodes.title: Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors
nodes.body:
• "__ Tinib"
  • IMATINIB (GLEEVEC)
    • MOA: competitively inhibits BCR-ABL T. Kinase in CML
    • → Also ↓KIT receptor: treatment for GIST

nodes.title: Ibrutinib
nodes.body:
• MOA: Inhibits Bruton Tyrosine Kinase (BTK) in the B-CELL receptor signal pathway necessary for B-cell proliferation
  • Tx for CLL

nodes.title: Proteosome Inhibitors
nodes.body:
• BORTEZOMIB (Velcade®)
    • → Tx for MULTIPLE MYELOMA

nodes.title: Immunomodulatory Agents
nodes.body:
• LENALIDOMIDE (Revlimid®)
    • → Tx for MULTIPLE MYELOMA
    • (MOA unclear)

nodes.title: Differentiating Agents
nodes.body:
• ATRA (All-trans Retinoic Acid)
  • MOA: Dissociates protein that blocks differentiation of promyelocytes → ↑neutrophils (granulocytes)
    • → Tx of APL
